arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Theodore Olson argued the federal statute explicitly preempts state requirements.
He stated the complaint challenges promotions of light cigarettes.
He claimed Congress preempted requirements respecting promotion based on health.
Justice Ginsburg questioned if states could sue over specific nicotine statements.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the boundary between federal and state consumer protection laws. It determines whether states can police false health claims. It affects how companies market products with health implications. It shapes the balance of regulatory power.
